guide.verdict: Easiest: Private app on your own workspace (self-serve, wait none). Hardest: Public app listed in the App Store (app review).

need_own_app.answer: Not for a prototype, since Composio can supply the Intercom OAuth app. For production with customers, use your own app for your branding, your own scopes, dedicated quota and shorter polling intervals.

prerequisites.title: Intercom developer account and customer agreement
prerequisites.detail: You must follow Intercom's registration requirements, and using the Intercom service itself requires its separate Subscription Terms of Service.

prerequisites.title: Test account or setup instructions for reviewers
prerequisites.detail: Reviewers test full functionality, so provide test credentials or setup instructions if your app needs an account.

prerequisites.title: Listing assets
prerequisites.detail: Prepare a 512x512 PNG icon, 2-5 images at least 1600x1000 PNG, terms and privacy URLs, and a support email. The name must be 40 characters or less and not contain 'Intercom'.

steps.title: Create app and enable OAuth
steps.detail: Create the app in the Developer Hub and tick Use OAuth on the Authentication page. Copy the client ID and secret from Basic Information.
steps.done_when: You hold the client ID and client secret.

steps.title: Draft minimal scope list with justifications
steps.detail: Choose only scopes the agent actually uses and write the reason for each. Over-privileged scopes are the top rejection reason.
steps.done_when: Each scope maps to a feature.

steps.title: Register HTTPS redirect URL
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard and add it under Redirect URLs. It must be HTTPS.
steps.done_when: The redirect URL is saved in the Developer Hub.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create a custom auth config via Composio's API with your client ID and secret.

steps.title: Record OAuth install and uninstall video
steps.detail: Show OAuth install, full app functionality and uninstall, with the full client_id and state visible in the OAuth URL.
steps.done_when: Video covers install, features and uninstall.

steps.title: Prepare listing content
steps.detail: Draft descriptions, categories, pricing model and checklist of image specs; the developer supplies images and legal URLs.

steps.title: Submit for review
steps.detail: Submit through the Test and publish pages in the Developer Hub.

steps.title: Wait for Intercom review
steps.detail: Review can take up to seven business days. If rejected, fix the issues and resubmit.

traps.title: Over-privileged scopes cause rejection
traps.detail: This is the most common reason for initial rejection. Intercom may also approve fewer permissions than requested, and credentials are limited to those.

traps.title: Region-specific authorization hosts
traps.detail: Intercom has three regional authorization hosts. Customers who sign in with Google fail on the wrong host.

traps.title: Composio callback domain cannot be verified by you
traps.detail: Intercom requires HTTPS redirect URLs. If you need your own domain on the callback, route it through your endpoint that 302-redirects to Composio's callback.

traps.title: Approval is at Intercom's discretion
traps.detail: Intercom may withhold approval at its sole discretion and may review or revoke credentials after approval.

traps.title: Broken installation links cause rejection
traps.detail: Listed apps must fill out the Installation status section; unclear links cause rejection.

blockers.symptom: Review rejection for scopes beyond current functionality
blockers.what_it_means: You requested scopes the app does not use.
blockers.what_to_do: Remove extra scopes and resubmit; allow up to seven business days again.
blockers.agent_can_help: Compare the scope list to the actual API calls and propose a minimal set.

blockers.what_it_means: The video did not show all functionality and the OAuth processes.
blockers.agent_can_help: Prepare a demo script covering install, features and uninstall.

open_questions: Is there an application fee or minimum customer count for App Store listing? Intercom reserves the right to charge fees; check the current Developer Hub or ask Intercom support.
Actual review time in practice: docs say up to seven business days, but a 2021 forum post reports 15 days without response. Ask Intercom developer support for current turnaround.
Does Composio's managed Intercom OAuth app work for outside customers without your own review? Not stated; check the Composio toolkit page.

evidence.quote: Providing broken or unclear links will result in an application rejection, and you will have to resubmit for review.
evidence.answer: A common rejection blocker is broken or unclear installation links in the Installation status section, which forces a resubmission.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: If you have requested scopes outside of the current functionality, you may be asked to adjust your scopes and resubmit the app.
evidence.answer: Requesting scopes beyond what the app actually uses is a blocker that can force scope changes and a resubmission.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: The only reason you would need to submit for review is if you wanted your app to be able to be installed in other workspaces.
evidence.answer: Intercom support told a developer (2022) that a private app for their own workspace needs no review; review is only needed for installs in other workspaces.
